messages:
alex: Heads-up — after adding more NVTX ranges to track per-request kernel selection and KV cache activity, our nightly nsys traces look way noisier and I'm seeing ~4-6% tail latency regression on small-batch inference. Anyone else see similar?

maria: saw that too. timeline has thousands of tiny ranges per token. NVTX overhead probably adding up, plus trace UI is unusable.

sam: can you paste one of the nsys captures or a screenshot? is the regression new or just visibility?

alex: regression correlates with the change that added per-op ranges in the runtime: we added ranges for kernel_select, kv_copy, kv_lookup, batch_merge. Before we only had per-request ranges. capture: `nsys profile -o run1 --trace=cuda,cublas,osrt python -m perf.run`

jun: quick thought: NVTX ranges themselves are cheap but not free. If you create ranges per token + per kernel + push/pop pairs very frequently you pay into the timing path and serialization into the CUPTI stream. On small batches that overhead is non-trivial.

maria: agree. two approaches: (1) coarsen ranges (group per-request phases), (2) convert super-fine ranges into instant markers (nvtxMarkA) for sampling traces, or (3) sample/conditional instrumentation.

sam: examples: instead of `nvtxRangePushA("kv:hit:request#%s:tok#%d")` do `nvtxRangePushA("kv:request#%s:phase:lookup")` and annotate hit/miss counts via counters in the console. Also add `nvtxNameCuDeviceA` for GPUs? (typo).

jun: minor nit: don't put unbounded request IDs into range names — they blow up the text size in traces and slow down the UI. Use short hex suffixes or hash: `req=0x5f2a`. Keep names <= ~64 chars.

alex: totally. wanted to propose a naming convention we can commit to. draft: 1) <subsystem>::<op>[:<short-req>]  e.g. `rt::kernel_select:0x5f2a` 2) coarse-grain spans for per-request phases: `rt::request:0x5f2a:prepare|kv|batch|dispatch` 3) only emit token-level spans when a debug flag is on.

maria: love that. also color-coding ranges helps when scanning. use NVTX colors for: prepare=0xFF8C00 (orange), kv=0x1E90FF (blue), kernel=0x32CD32 (green).

sam: for kernel-selection we should annotate which kernel path was chosen (fp16 vs q4_0 vs q8_0) and whether we used an optimized fused attention kernel. e.g. `rt::kernel_select:fp16:fused_attn` — but again keep req truncated if included.

jun: instrumentation for KV cache: two spans: `kv::lookup` (readonly, short) and `kv::copy_out` (memcopy to device). If you want counts: emit a single `nvtxRangePushA("kv:request:0x5f2a:lookup")` and inside increment a counters map we expose to the console. Avoid pushing a range per shard per token.

alex: profiling notes I collected: 
- nsys command we used: `nsys profile -o nvtx_debug --trace=cuda,cublas,cudnn,osrt --capture-range=nvtx python -m perf.run` — `--capture-range=nvtx` lets NVTX control capture windows.
- perfetto: export `nsys probe` output to Chrome trace for quick timeline scraping.
- when checking hot kernels, focus on cublasGemmEx / custom attention kernel durations and the kernel queue gaps.

maria: for kernel timelines, we should tag the kernel launch with a small NVTX push showing kernel name and the selected tile size or algorithm index. Example snippet: ```c
nvtxRangePushA("kernel::matmul:algo=3:tile=64x64");
launch_matmul(...);
nvtxRangePop();
```

sam: Also useful: mark the decision point separately: `nvtxRangePushA("kernel_decide:matmul")` then `nvtxRangePushA("kernel_exec:matmul:algo=3")`. This separates selection cost from execution cost in the trace.

jun: regarding sampling to reduce noise: add a random sampling gate in runtime: only emit per-token ranges for 1/N requests (configurable). For example `if (rand() % sample_rate == 0) emit_token_spans=true;` Also provide an env var to force always-on for debugging.

alex: CI note: cc @ci-bot — we should add a performance test flag that enables coarse NVTX in nightly runs and a separate debug job that runs with fine-grained NVTX + perf capture. We want to detect regressions caused by instrumentation.

ci-bot: added perf-nvtx-debug pipeline (opt-in) — see: https://ci.internal/redwood/perf/pipelines/1234 :white_check_mark:

maria: side point — NVTX names with `:` are fine but perfetto categorization sometimes treats `:` specially; prefer `::` as namespace separator (as alex suggested) to be consistent.

sam: one more practical trick: use `nvtxDomain_t` to group annotations so UI can toggle visibility per-domain. That way you can hide `token` domain when viewing standard traces.

jun: troubleshooting checklist for the regression: 1) re-run nsys with NVTX turned off to get baseline; 2) run NVTX-on trace with coarse ranges; 3) run sampled fine-grain trace to validate overhead; 4) compare kernel launch counts and wall time distribution.

alex: i've attached a tiny example diff we can land to reduce noise: - convert per-token `kv:hit` ranges to counters + single `kv:request` span - add `RT_NVTX_SAMPLE_RATE` env var default 128 - truncate request ids in names to 6 hex chars - add domain `RT_TOKEN` for optional toggling

maria: sounds good. can you open a PR with that diff and add unit test that verifies truncated naming and sample gating?

alex: on it. I'll also add a short README in eng-runtime docs with the NVTX naming rules and sample nsys/perfetto commands.

sam: thanks — once PR is up i'll run a few local captures and share before/after numbers. :rocket:

jun: fwiw, if we still see regressions after coarsening, we should audit any synchronous host-side logging we added alongside NVTX. Logging + NVTX can amplify stalls.

alex: good call. i'll double-check. thanks y'all! :thumbsup:
